answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08, d1a14h2 (sunid 343393, PDB 1a14 chain H residues 1-8) is not a real protein domain. It is an N-terminal tag/leader segment in class l (Artifacts) > fold l.1 (Tags) > superfamily l.1.1 (Tags) > family l.1.1.1 (Tags) > protein 'N-terminal Tags' > species 'Synthetic'. The sccs is l.1.1.1. The remaining residues 9-111, d1a14h1, are the real antibody VH domain (b.1.1.1, Immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich / Immunoglobulin / V set domains; protein: immunoglobulin heavy chain variable domain, VH; mouse). Its homology is implied at superfamily level and it is part of Fab NC10 (only Fv coordinates included). Similarity to the l.1.1.1 tag segment should NOT be treated as protein homology evidence. The service flags it with the warning 'artifact_not_homology_evidence': class l holds artificial sequence artifacts, so similarity to these records does not imply biological homology. Homology_implied_by_level is false for d1a14h2. A short tag match is typically an expression, purification or linker artifact shared by unrelated proteins. It gives no evidence of common ancestry, function or fold. Any homology inference for chain H should rest on d1a14h1 (the VH domain, b.1.1.1) and not on the 8-residue tag. Hits should not be used for classification, templates or function transfer, and the tag region should be masked or excluded in sequence or structure searches. Caveat: the tag sequence itself could not be retrieved (the sequence endpoint returned 404 for d1a14h2), so the answer rests on the SCOPe lineage and annotation records.
